The FOMC statement underscores a solid macro backdrop—strong job gains, low unemployment, inflation near 2 percent, and an accommodative stance with balanced risks and a gradual hiking path. The contemporaneous Beige Book broadly corroborates this: most Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth, tight labor markets with gradually building wage pressures, and generally optimistic business outlooks. It also notes some offsets—rising input costs (including steel/aluminum), capacity and transportation bottlenecks, and mixed consumer spending in categories like autos—yet bank contacts cited steady-to-stronger loan demand with largely unchanged standards and healthy credit quality, aligning with SLOOS and suggesting credit supply remains supportive. On net, the Beige Book modestly reinforces the positive tone while flagging manageable constraints, warranting a slight positive tilt.
